title: Exact functors commute with derived limits of towers
statement:
Use the pro-etale module-sheaf and tower categories of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] for two coefficient data on schemes $T$ and $S$. Write $\mathcal D_T=D(\operatorname{Mod}(A_T))$ and $\mathcal D_S=D(\operatorname{Mod}(B_S))$, with derived categories as in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $F:\mathcal D_T\to\mathcal D_S$ be an exact additive triangulated functor [def-weil-triangulated-category], with shift comparison $\xi_K:F(K[1])\xrightarrow{\sim}F(K)[1]$. Its compatibility with levelwise evaluation means that an action $\widetilde F:D(\operatorname{Tow}_A(T))\to D(\operatorname{Tow}_B(S))$ is supplied, together with natural isomorphisms $\operatorname{ev}_n\widetilde F\cong F\operatorname{ev}_n$ that respect the transition maps. Assume that for every countable family $(K_n)$ in $\mathcal D_T$ the canonical product comparison
$$\phi_{(K_n)}:F(\prod_n K_n)\longrightarrow\prod_nF(K_n),\qquad \mathrm{pr}'_n\phi_{(K_n)}=F(\mathrm{pr}_n),$$
is an isomorphism; the products here are products in the derived categories [def-weil-category-product], not products of abelian sheaves before derivation.

Let $M_\bullet\in D(\operatorname{Tow}_A(T))$, put $M_n=\operatorname{ev}_nM_\bullet$, and put $N_\bullet=\widetilde F(M_\bullet)$. Use the evaluation isomorphisms to write $N_n=F(M_n)$, with transitions $F(t_n)$ for $t_n:M_{n+1}\to M_n$. Choose Roos triangles for $L=\Rlim M_\bullet$ and $L'=\Rlim N_\bullet$ as in [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-limit, def-weil-derived-limit]:
$$L\xrightarrow p P\xrightarrow{1-s}P\xrightarrow\delta L[1],\qquad L'\xrightarrow{p'}P'\xrightarrow{1-s'}P'\xrightarrow{\delta'}L'[1],$$
where $P=\prod_nM_n$, $P'=\prod_nF(M_n)$ and $s,s'$ are the shifts of [def-weil-tower-transition-endomorphism]. Write $\phi=\phi_{(M_n)}$. Then applying $F$ to the first triangle and identifying $F(P)$ with $P'$ via $\phi$ gives a Roos triangle for the evaluated image tower. In particular $F(L)$ is a derived limit of $(F(M_n),F(t_n))$. There exists a morphism $c:F(L)\to L'$ such that
$$p'c=\phi F(p),\qquad c[1]\xi_LF(\delta)=\delta'\phi,$$
and every such $c$ is an isomorphism. Thus $F(\Rlim M_\bullet)\cong\Rlim\widetilde F(M_\bullet)$ as objects, compatibly with the Roos triangles. The bare triangulated data assert neither a unique comparison $c$ nor a canonical choice of it; any independently specified comparison satisfying these two equations is an isomorphism.

proof.text: By [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-limit], evaluating $M_\bullet$ gives the inverse system $(M_n,t_n)$ in $\mathcal D_T$. The transition-compatible evaluation identifications for $\widetilde F$ give $(F(M_n),F(t_n))$ for $N_\bullet$. Apply the triangle clause of [prop-weil-pbc-roos-triangle] to $M_\bullet$ and to $N_\bullet$: it gives exactly the two distinguished triangles displayed in the statement, with $L$ and $L'$ in their first positions. Denote the projections of $P$ and $P'$ by $\pi_n$ and $\rho_n$.

source.place: Tag 08TC (definition-derived-limit); the functorial strict-tower Roos triangle is the stated input prop-weil-pbc-roos-triangle.

proof.text: The product comparison has $\rho_n\phi=F(\pi_n)$, and the shifts satisfy $\pi_ns=t_n\pi_{n+1}$ and $\rho_ns'=F(t_n)\rho_{n+1}$ by [def-weil-tower-transition-endomorphism]. Hence $\rho_n\phi F(s)=F(\pi_ns)=F(t_n)F(\pi_{n+1})=\rho_ns'\phi$ for every $n$. Product uniqueness [def-weil-category-product] gives $\phi F(s)=s'\phi$. Since exact functors here are additive by [def-weil-triangulated-category], $F(1-s)=1-F(s)$, and therefore $\phi F(1-s)=(1-s')\phi$. This verifies the middle square using all transition maps, rather than just identifying the two product objects.

source.place: Tag 08TC (definition-derived-limit), formula for the transition endomorphism; Tag 014V (definition-exact-functor-triangulated-categories).

proof.text: Exactness in [def-weil-triangulated-category] sends the source Roos triangle to the distinguished triangle $F(L)\xrightarrow{F(p)}F(P)\xrightarrow{F(1-s)}F(P)\xrightarrow{\xi_LF(\delta)}F(L)[1]$. Set $a=\phi F(p)$ and $b=\xi_LF(\delta)\phi^{-1}$. Step 2 and these definitions make $(\mathrm{id}_{F(L)},\phi,\phi)$ an isomorphism from this triangle to $F(L)\xrightarrow aP'\xrightarrow{1-s'}P'\xrightarrow bF(L)[1]$. The latter triangle is distinguished by TR1, and so [def-weil-derived-limit] says precisely that $F(L)$, with these maps, is a derived limit of the image sequence. No identification of cones has been chosen here.

Rotate the triangle of step 3 and the target Roos triangle once, using TR2 of [def-weil-triangulated-category]. They become $P'\xrightarrow{1-s'}P'\xrightarrow bF(L)[1]\xrightarrow{-a[1]}P'[1]$ and $P'\xrightarrow{1-s'}P'\xrightarrow{\delta'}L'[1]\xrightarrow{-p'[1]}P'[1]$. Apply TR3 to the identity maps on the first two vertices. It gives $u:F(L)[1]\to L'[1]$ satisfying $ub=\delta'$ and $p'[1]u=a[1]$. Since the shift is an automorphism, write $u=c[1]$ and unshift the second equality to obtain $p'c=a$. Substitute the definitions of $a,b$ and multiply $c[1]b=\delta'$ on the right by $\phi$ to obtain exactly the two comparison equations in the statement. This establishes existence, without asserting uniqueness.

source.place: Tag 0145 (definition-triangulated-category), TR2 and TR3; Tag 0H9J (remark-functoriality-derived-limit), completion of a product square without uniqueness.

proof.text: For any $c$ satisfying the two comparison equations, step 2 supplies the remaining square. Thus $(c,\phi,\phi)$ is a morphism from the distinguished image under $F$ of the source triangle to the distinguished target triangle, including the connecting-map square with $c[1]$. Both product components are isomorphisms by hypothesis. Apply [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso] to conclude that its first component $c$ is an isomorphism. This applies to the comparison produced in step 4 and to every other comparison satisfying the displayed equations.

split_report.summary: STATEMENT-DISPUTED: a triangulated functor alone does not specify a canonical comparison between chosen Roos cones. Repaired the type of the evaluation compatibility by spelling out the tower action, and replaced the unsupported canonical-choice assertion by existence of a Roos-triangle comparison and invertibility of every such comparison. Five steps use only existing nodes: the Roos triangle, an explicit product-projection identity, exact image and isomorphism of triangles, TR2/TR3 completion, and the two-out-of-three triangle theorem. No new nodes; all original blueprint/import fields preserved.
split_report.blueprint: Original proof paragraph 1 is step 1. Original paragraph 2, applying F and identifying 1-s, is steps 2-3. Its final false sentence about canonical cone isomorphisms is repaired by steps 4-5. The compact-support unit route through finite reductions and Roos triangles is retained.
